text:
Predicates:
DeadlyDisease(x) ::: x is a deadly disease.
LowSurvivalRate(x) ::: x comes with a low survival rate.
SevereCancer(x) ::: x is a severe cancer.
BileDuctCancer(x) ::: x is bile duct cancer.
Cholangiocarcinoma(x) ::: x is Cholangiocarcinoma.
MildFlu(x) ::: x is mild flu.
ColorectalCancer(x) ::: x is colorectal cancer.
FormOf(x, y) ::: x is a form of y.
KindOf(x, y) ::: x is a kind of y.

Premises:
∀x (DeadlyDisease(x) → LowSurvivalRate(x)) ::: If something is a deadly disease, then it comes with a low survival rate.
SevereCancer(x) → DeadlyDisease(x) ::: Severe cancers are deadly diseases.
BileDuctCancer(bileDuctCancer) ::: Bile duct cancer is bile duct cancer.
∀x (Cholangiocarcinoma(x) → BileDuctCancer(x)) ::: All Cholangiocarcinoma is bile duct cancer.
MildFlu(mildFlu) ::: Mild flu comes with a low survival rate.
ColorectalCancer(cancer) ∧ ¬(BileDuctCancer(cancer) ∧ LowSurvivalRate(cancer)) ::: Colorectal cancer is not both a bile duct cancer and with a low survival rate.

Conclusion:
FormOf(cancer, Cholangiocarcinoma) ∧ (KindOf(cancer, MildFlu) ∨ KindOf(cancer, BileDuctCancer) ∨ (FormOf(cancer, Cholangiocarcinoma) ∧ KindOf(cancer, MildFlu)))
